hero.description: Nimbus is the operations platform for product teams: auth, roles, notifications, and analytics wired together on day one, so your first sprint goes into the thing customers actually pay for.

features.heading: Everything the boring half of your product needs
features.description: The parts every serious app grows anyway — identity, permissions, notifications, telemetry — designed once and shared across your whole workspace.

auth.title: Auth that already works
auth.description: Email, OAuth, magic links, and password recovery on day one — sessions handled, invite-only or open signup by config.

roles.title: Roles and permissions
roles.description: Permissions ride in the token and are enforced at the database. The UI hides what a user cannot do; the row-level policy makes sure of it.

notifications.title: Realtime notifications
notifications.description: An in-app center and toasts fed by a live subscription, so a grant, a mention, or a failed job lands the moment it happens.

analytics.title: Analytics you can theme
analytics.description: Charts wired to your design tokens, so light mode, dark mode, and a rebrand are one variable change — never a redraw.

automations.title: Automations and webhooks
automations.description: Schedule work, react to events, and fan out to third parties from a service that holds the secrets your browser should not.

performance.title: Fast by construction
performance.description: Server-rendered, hydrated with event replay, and shipped as a single bundle per route — quick on the first paint and the tenth click.

howItWorks.heading: From empty repo to production in an afternoon
howItWorks.description: No migration project, no rewrite. Point Nimbus at your database, invite your team, and keep shipping.

connect.title: Connect your data
connect.description: One command links your Postgres schema. Types are generated from the database, so a column rename fails the build instead of production.

invite.title: Invite your team
invite.description: Assign roles from the admin console. Every grant is audited, and revoking access signs the person out everywhere.

ship.title: Ship the product
ship.description: Compose your screens from the shared component library and let the platform handle the parts nobody demos.

testimonials.heading: Teams stopped rebuilding the same four systems

rafael.quote: The permissions model is the first one our security reviewer signed off on without a follow-up meeting. Checks live in the database, not in a component nobody remembers.

nina.quote: Design shipped a new palette on a Tuesday and every chart, badge, and dark-mode surface followed. That used to be a two-sprint migration for us.

pricing.heading: Priced per seat, not per surprise
pricing.description: Every plan includes the full platform. You pay for the size of your team and the scale of your workload — nothing is gated behind a sales call except the things that genuinely need one.

faq.heading: Questions we get before the first call
faq.weAnswer: — we answer within a business day.

database.question: Do I have to move my database?
database.answer: No. Nimbus connects to your existing Postgres and generates types from your schema. Your data stays where it is, and you keep every extension and migration you already rely on.

permissions.question: How are permissions actually enforced?
permissions.answer: Permissions are stamped into the access token and enforced by row-level security in the database. The UI uses the same claims to decide what to render, but the database is the thing that says no.

revoke.question: What happens when I revoke access?
revoke.answer: The grant is removed and audited immediately, and disabling a user signs them out of every session globally rather than waiting for a token to expire.

designSystem.question: Can I use my own design system?
designSystem.answer: Yes. Every surface reads from a small set of design tokens, so a palette change or a font swap propagates through components, charts, and dark mode without touching a component file.

freeTier.question: Is there a free tier for side projects?
freeTier.answer: Starter is free for up to five people and 10,000 automated runs a month, with no card required. Most side projects never leave it.

downtime.question: How do you handle downtime?
downtime.answer: Growth and Enterprise plans publish a rolling uptime figure and a public status page. Enterprise adds a 99.99% SLA with service credits and a named contact during incidents.
